references.title: Vacuum Thermionic Work Functions of Polycrystalline Be, Ti, Cr, Fe, Ni, Cu, Pt, and Type 304 Stainless Steel
references.primary_access: publisher-deposited Crossref abstract; NASA NTRS19660053343 bibliographic record; full publisher article inaccessible
references.support: Effective thermionic work function 4.3 eV for well-outgassed polycrystalline 304 in clean 1e-9 Torr vacuum. This is not an oxide/water-coated pulsed-surface calibration.

references.title: The effect of a magnetic field on the motion of electrons for the field emission process description
references.authors: S. O. Lebedynskyi; V. I. Miroshnichenko; R. I. Kholodov; V. A. Baturin
references.primary_access: complete publisher PDF; page64 equations21–30 visually inspected
references.support: Minimal-coupling Hamiltonian contains (p_z-e B_t x)^2/(2m). Expanding relative to x=0 yields a signed cross term plus positive quadratic term. The census retains the existing absolute-speed upper bound; it is not a measured correction to current. Collinear-field separation and the E = 100 MV/m, B = 1 T example do not validate the code cutoff 0.2 for this weak-field thermal case.

references.title: Electric charges on stainless steel surfaces: The effects of hydrogen, charged particles, illumination, and electric fields on the work function
references.authors: R. J. D’Arcy; N. A. Surplice
references.support: UHV vibrating-capacitor measurements show reversible work-function changes with illumination, charged particles and electric fields, consistent with oxide-state charge trapping. No pulse-specific calibrated SS304 surface model follows from this abstract.

references.title: Field Emission from Bismuth and Tungsten in a Magnetic Field
references.authors: R. F. Waites; H. A. Schwettman
references.support: No dc quantum current variations above 0.5 percent observed for bismuth/tungsten up to 45 kG in the studied geometry. These different materials and longitudinal quantum-supply experiment do not qualify crossed-field SS304 near-barrier launch or authorize guard relaxation.
